claims.text: Hormuz is a CLI-first AI gateway and control plane that sits between existing Codex or Claude Code clients and OpenAI or Anthropic provider APIs.
Hormuz applies identity-bound client, model, output-limit, token-budget, and estimated-cost policy before provider egress.
Hormuz can redact or deny configured and detected secret values before upstream serialization and records only content-free detection evidence.
Hormuz records versioned metadata-only policy, usage, cost, status, and security evidence while excluding prompt and response bodies from its usage ledger.

The hormuz demo command exercises the real HTTP, policy, redaction, request-attempt, and SQLite evidence path against disposable loopback providers without a provider account or external provider call.

Pinned Codex 0.147.0 and Claude Code 2.1.233 clients are exercised through Hormuz in blocking simulator CI, and one same-revision content-free live artifact verifies governed streaming calls through real OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints.
Hormuz reports metadata-only token and estimated-cost usage by organization, team, person, client, and model, with explicit pricing and coverage boundaries.
Employee credentials are removed before provider egress, provider credentials stay on the Hormuz service, and prompt or response bodies are not written to the usage database.

Hormuz's public alpha is self-hosted, does not operate a hosted customer-data service, leaves database export, retention, backup, restore, and deletion to customer operators, and makes no universal-erasure claim across provider, IdP, KMS, Object Lock, backup, or observability systems.

Hormuz v0.1.3 is published as signed linux/amd64 OCI digest sha256:8ac24f5c7afb8ce09ec133616de06702f568a2e70594d8034146a131d86e5b67 with anonymous GHCR pull, exact-workflow verification, a public-Rekor image signature, and registry SBOM and SLSA attestations; GHCR remains the first registry rather than the portable artifact contract, and the documented mirror procedure requires recursive copying and destination verification.

Exact account-free proofs cover a single-VM Compose pilot, multi-replica Kubernetes and Helm application operation, CloudNativePG failover and quorum loss, and a disaster-recovery rehearsal within its accepted reference targets; these bounded references are not production certification, a customer SLA, or broad platform portability.

Hormuz v0.1.3 is a public open-source alpha for evaluation and tester-led hardening, not a production certification, universal HA or disaster-recovery guarantee, compliance claim, customer SLA, or independent security review.

analytics.definition: An independent evaluator reports that a clean supported-environment install completed and hormuz --help exited successfully.
analytics.privacy_boundary: No hidden CLI telemetry and no prompts, responses, credentials, or customer identifiers.

analytics.definition: An independent evaluator reports that hormuz demo completed with every documented PASS line.
analytics.privacy_boundary: Record release or commit and outcome only; never demo inputs or local paths.

analytics.definition: An opted-in evaluator confirms at least one synthetic or authorized request reached a provider through Hormuz with a recorded policy outcome.
analytics.privacy_boundary: Aggregate count and provider family only; never prompt, response, credential, or employee identity.

analytics.definition: An opted-in evaluator reports meaningful Hormuz use in two distinct seven-day periods.
analytics.privacy_boundary: No cross-site fingerprinting or automatic CLI identity; deduplicate only with explicit consent.

analytics.definition: A public issue, discussion, or private security report leads to a confirmed documentation, compatibility, security, or product improvement.
analytics.privacy_boundary: Count classification and resolution only; keep private reports and personal data out of launch analytics.

analytics.definition: A human completes a substantive governance discovery conversation with an organization that matches the stated alpha boundary.
analytics.privacy_boundary: Report aggregate stage counts publicly; customer identity and notes remain private.

analytics.definition: A human submits the owner-approved paid-pilot application and consents to follow-up.
analytics.privacy_boundary: Collect the minimum contact and qualification fields; never request credentials, prompts, responses, or customer data.
